summary: A public plugin contract threads every method and one exported field through a package-local `any` alias, forcing an unchecked assertion into every method of every plugin; the clean version types the interface in the plugin's own state, keeps the heterogeneous registry that made erasure necessary, and moves the erasure to one unexported adapter reached only through a generic Register shell.
notes: Two things about this pair are load-bearing and neither is obvious from a diff. FIRST: the dirty fixture spells its erasure `State`, a package-local `type State any` alias, not a bare `any` in the signatures. That is how the founding evidence spelled it (candace/pkg/widget/sdk.go:24), and a detector that only matched a literal `any` would report nothing here — so this fixture is also the regression test for the scanner's alias resolution. The exported `Entry.Current any` field is deliberately spelled the other way, so the pair covers both spellings and both member kinds (interface method and struct field); dirty_min_findings is 2 rather than 1 for that reason. Note the alias must be written `type State any` and never `type State interface{}` — the latter is a named interface declaration and would fire CS-1, breaking the case's isolation. SECOND: the clean fixture deliberately contains NO exported `any`, not even the genuinely unknown-shape kind CS-7 permits. This is the third instance of the collision CS-5 hit first and CS-6 hit second: the heuristic flags every exported bare `any` in a non-internal package, a permitted JSON-envelope field is exactly that shape, and the runner requires that nothing at all fires on a clean fixture. Narrowing the heuristic to auto-detect 'genuinely unknown shape' was rejected as impossible — no lexer can tell a JSON envelope from an erased contract — and a marker comment was rejected as an escape hatch the gate would then be graded on. So CS-7 splits across the tiers exactly as CS-5 and CS-6 do: the shape is tier 1 (here), the judgment is tier 2 (case 025-erasure-judgment, whose correct answer keeps an `any`). See ../../README.md § 'When a rule's exemption cannot live in a fixture'. Note finally that the clean fixture keeps `iErasedPlugin` and `erasedPlugin[S]` unexported: that is not a trick to dodge the gate but the rule itself, since CS-7 governs public contracts and an unexported adapter is precisely where the erasure is supposed to live.
